# ECN 4199 — Industrial Data Analytics

---

# Activity Information

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Week | Week 6 |
| Topic | Interactive Dashboards and Data Storytelling |
| Marks | 5 Marks |
| Duration | 1 Hour |
| Attempts | One Attempt Only |
| Access | Lecturer Passcode Required |

---

# Instructions

1. Open the Week 6 live notebook.
2. Save a copy to your Google Drive.
3. Complete all required tasks.
4. Answer all interpretation questions.
5. Submit before the activity closes.

---

# Important Reminder

This activity tests:

- interactive visualization
- dashboard design
- Plotly usage
- data storytelling
- interpretation
- economic communication

The goal is NOT to create decorative dashboards.

The goal is to communicate economic insights clearly and analytically.

---

# Task 1 — Create Interactive Inflation Graph

## Objective

Build an interactive inflation trend graph.

---

## Instructions

Create an interactive Plotly line graph showing inflation over time.

---

## Expected Structure

```python
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

data = pd.read_csv("sri_lanka_macro.csv")

fig = px.line(data,
              x="Year",
              y="Inflation",
              title="Inflation Trends")

fig.show()
```

---

## Questions

### Question 1

When does inflation increase sharply?

---

### Question 2

What economic conditions might explain this increase?

---

### Question 3

Why are interactive graphs useful compared to static graphs?

---

# Task 2 — Interactive GDP Growth Bar Chart

## Objective

Compare GDP growth visually.

---

## Instructions

Create an interactive bar chart for GDP growth.

---

## Example Structure

```python
fig = px.bar(data,
             x="Year",
             y="GDP_Growth",
             color="GDP_Growth")

fig.show()
```

---

## Questions

### Question 1

Which year had the worst GDP growth?

---

### Question 2

Why are bar charts useful for comparisons?

---

### Question 3

Why should colors be used carefully in dashboards?

---

# Task 3 — Scatter Plot and Relationships

## Objective

Explore relationships between macroeconomic variables.

---

## Instructions

Create an interactive scatter plot using:

- Inflation
- Exchange_Rate_Change

Add hover information using Year.

---

## Example Structure

```python
fig = px.scatter(data,
                 x="Inflation",
                 y="Exchange_Rate_Change",
                 hover_name="Year")

fig.show()
```

---

## Questions

### Question 1

Do inflation and exchange rate changes appear related?

---

### Question 2

Are there outliers?

---

### Question 3

What macroeconomic events might explain extreme observations?

---

# Task 4 — Build Mini Dashboard

## Objective

Combine multiple indicators into one analytical system.

---

## Instructions

Create a mini dashboard including:

- inflation
- GDP growth
- exchange rate change

---

## Suggested Dashboard Structure

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| Top | Inflation trend |
| Middle | GDP growth comparison |
| Bottom | Scatter plot relationship |

---

## Question

What overall macroeconomic story does your dashboard communicate?

Write short interpretation.

---

# Task 5 — Dashboard Design Evaluation

## Objective

Critically evaluate dashboard quality.

---

## Questions

### Question 1

Why is too much information dangerous in dashboard design?

---

### Question 2

What makes a dashboard easy to understand?

---

### Question 3

Why is dashboard design important for policymakers and economists?

---

# Reflection Question

Write a short paragraph answering:

```text
Why is economic storytelling important even when AI tools can generate dashboards automatically?
```

Your answer should include:

- interpretation
- communication
- policy relevance
- limitations of automated visualization

---

# Mini Quiz

## Question 1

What is the primary purpose of a dashboard?

A. Decoration  
B. Programming practice  
C. Decision support and communication  
D. File storage  

---

## Question 2

Which library is mainly used this week?

A. NumPy  
B. Plotly  
C. Statsmodels  
D. TensorFlow  

---

## Question 3

What can users do in interactive visualizations?

A. Hover and zoom  
B. Delete data automatically  
C. Install software  
D. Remove variables  

---

## Question 4

Which graph type is best for time trends?

A. Pie chart  
B. Histogram  
C. Line graph  
D. Table  

---

# Submission Instructions

Before submitting:

1. Save notebook properly.
2. Rename notebook using:

```text
Week06_IndexNumber_Name.ipynb
```

Example:

```text
Week06_2024BA12345_Perera.ipynb
```

3. Set notebook sharing to:

```text
Anyone with the link → Viewer
```

---

# Submission Link

[Submit Week 6 Activity](PASTE_WEEK6_SUBMISSION_LINK_HERE)

---

# Passcode Access

The lecturer will provide the passcode during the lecture.

Students without the correct passcode cannot access the submission form.

---

# Common Errors

## Problem 1 — Too Many Graphs

More graphs do NOT necessarily improve analysis.

Simplify.

---

## Problem 2 — Missing Labels

Every graph must include:

- title
- labels
- readable structure

---

## Problem 3 — Random Colors

Colors should communicate meaning.

Do not use colors randomly.

---

## Problem 4 — Weak Interpretation

Dashboards without interpretation are incomplete analysis.

---

## Problem 5 — Misleading Visual Design

Poor scaling or clutter can distort economic understanding.

---

# Academic Integrity

Students may use lecture materials and course notes.

However:

- copied answers are not allowed
- copied notebooks are not allowed
- AI-generated answers without understanding are unacceptable

Students are responsible for all submitted work.
